document_check.note: The document is Chen Y, Qi Y, Hu Y, et al., Li T, Le W (ADNI), 'Integrated cerebellar radiomic-network model for predicting mild cognitive impairment in Alzheimer's disease', Alzheimer's Dement 2025;21:e14361. It develops cerebellar and hippocampal radiomic models in ADNI (n = 1319) with an in-house test set (n = 308) and an NC-to-MCI conversion analysis (n = 371). Table 2 and the conversion AUCs match the cited statements.

cited_result: The principal cited result is the comparative discrimination of cerebellar vs hippocampal radiomic-network models (Table 2, p. 11). For MCI vs NC, the cerebellar model scored AUC 0.94 in training and 0.86 in testing, against 0.69 and 0.72 for the hippocampal model. For AD vs NC and AD vs MCI, hippocampal AUCs were higher, with DeLong P significant in training only (test P = 0.200 and 0.157). A second cited result is the NC-to-MCI conversion AUC: 0.818 cerebellar vs 0.659 hippocampal, with no test reported (p. 12).
tool_reason: The cited results are the discrimination (AUC) and ranking of machine-learning diagnostic and prognostic models, so PROBAST applies, with the PROBAST+AI considerations.

domains.rationale: The diagnostic groups were sampled separately, which is a case-control design. The in-house NC came partly from a physical examination centre and patients from neurology. Inclusion and exclusion criteria appear only in the supplement. The conversion analysis was restricted to NC participants who completed 72 months of follow-up.

domains.rationale: There were 2730 cerebellar candidate features. Univariable p < 0.05 filtering and LASSO appear to have been run on the whole ADNI set before 5-fold CV, so the training estimates leak information. The best of ten classifiers was chosen per task on unstated grounds. No calibration is reported. Site harmonisation is not reported. Training AUCs near 0.998 fell to 0.83-0.90 on the test set, which shows optimism, and the only significant hippocampal advantages come from these training estimates. The conversion AUCs follow forward stepwise selection in 371 completers with no validation described, and the Kaplan-Meier cut-offs used test data. The in-house set is an independent external test for the Table 2 models, which is a strength.

overall_rationale: The participants domain is high risk because of case-control sampling of diagnostic groups and the completers-only conversion cohort. The analysis domain is high risk because of univariable feature filtering before CV, a very high feature-to-event ratio, per-task classifier selection, no calibration, clear training optimism and unvalidated stepwise conversion models. The outcome domain is unclear because the criteria sit in the supplement.

applicability.rationale: The groups have a case-control spectrum. The in-house NC were recruited from a physical examination centre and patients from a neurology department in one Chinese hospital, while ADNI participants are research volunteers.
The predictors are standard 3 T T1 MRI radiomics, although texture features may not transfer across scanners without harmonisation.
The outcome is clinical NC/MCI/AD labels whose criteria are not given in the main text.
